angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 6,303,042 km at 10.36 pc = 8.14 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 62509: the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 96.54 +/- 0.27 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b): 10.358 +/- 0.029 pc; Gaia DR3 cannot see the star
radiusSource: Radius 9.06 +/- 0.03 solar radii from Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 62509: radius 9.06 +/- 0.03 solar radii (Table 5), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 8.134 +/- 0.013 mas (NPOI, Table 4) and the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b): 6,303,042 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.91 +/- 0.09 solar masses from Hatzes et al. (2012), A&A 543, A98, abstract: M = 1.91 +/- 0.09 solar masses from the p-mode frequency spacing (7.14 +/- 0.12 microHz) and the interferometric radius (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/201219332); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4586 +/- 57 K from Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 62509: effective temperature 4586 +/- 57 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 62509: effective temperature 4586 +/- 57 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/pollux.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 2.805, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue, table 5 (320-1080 nm, 2.5 nm steps, 10 nm resolution, absolute flux in W m^-2 m^-1)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
